title: Find a bug and protect the fix with tests
outcome: Repair an order decision and prove that rejected orders stay rejected.
story: The shop sometimes ships an unpaid order. Amina needs you to reproduce the problem, fix the actual rule, and keep a test that catches it if it returns.

frames.explanation: A comparison checks payment; an assignment accidentally changes it.
The business rule includes 5000, so the boundary uses >=.

sections.title: Start with evidence
paragraphs: Debugging means finding why a program behaves differently from its intended rules. Write down the input, expected result, and actual result before changing the code. A reproducible example lets another person see the same problem.

Our fictional rule says: ship a paid order worth at least 5000 cents; otherwise hold it. An unpaid order worth 6000 cents should be held. If the program ships it, its payment condition needs investigation.

sections.title: Read the suspicious line
paragraphs: The equals sign = assigns a value. The comparison === asks whether two values are equal. A line using payment = "paid" can change the input while the program is trying to decide what it means.

Repair the reason for the wrong result rather than special-casing one example. A fix that rejects only the exact amount 6000 leaves the same payment bug at other amounts. A good test should make the intended rule visible.

sections.title: Protect the boundary
paragraphs: At least 5000 includes exactly 5000. The operator >= expresses that rule. The operator > excludes the exact boundary. Test an amount just below, exactly at, and just above the threshold.

Negative and fractional-cent amounts are outside this exercise’s contract. Reject them with RangeError before considering shipping. This protects the decision from strange but apparently successful outputs.

sections.title: Keep a regression test
paragraphs: A regression is a previously fixed problem returning after a change. A regression test keeps the reproducing example and its expected result. Run it whenever the code changes.

A passing suite is evidence about the cases it covers. It cannot prove every possible behaviour is correct. Add a case when you discover a new failure, and explain which rule that case protects. The independent project asks you to write a new case of your own.

words.meaning: Finding the cause of a difference between expected and actual behaviour.
A test that catches a known problem if it returns.
The exact point where a rule starts or stops applying.

The actual result exposes the incorrect addition.

exercise.title: Stop shipping unpaid orders
exercise.brief: Repair decideShipment(amountCents, payment). A paid order of at least 5000 cents ships; other valid orders are held. Reject negative or fractional amounts.

steps.title: Fix the payment comparison
steps.task: An unpaid order must remain unpaid. Compare payment with "paid" rather than assigning a new value.

steps.title: Fix the threshold boundary
steps.task: Include exactly 5000 cents. Keep amounts below 5000 on hold.

steps.title: Reject unacceptable amounts
steps.task: Add the amount contract before the shipping decision. Reject negative or non-whole cents using RangeError.
steps.hint: Use Number.isInteger(amountCents) and amountCents < 0 before the payment rule.

project.title: A regression repair report
project.brief: Deliver the shipping fix with evidence another developer can reproduce. Preserve the unpaid-order case and add one case you chose yourself.
deliverables: The corrected function and regression cases.
A short repair report explaining the cause.

milestones.title: Reproduce the bug
actions: Show expected hold and observed ship before the repair.

milestones.title: Repair the rule
actions: Correct the exact threshold and validation.

milestones.title: Protect and explain
actions: Add a new test and explain what it covers.

acceptance: A paid qualifying order still ships.
